name: xss-prevention
description: Prevent cross-site scripting by enforcing output encoding, CSP headers, and safe DOM manipulation
author: community
content:
## XSS Prevention Never insert untrusted data into HTML without proper encoding or sanitization (OWASP A03:2021 Injection). ### Rules - Always encode output based on context: HTML body, HTML attribute, JavaScript, CSS, URL - Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `document.write()`, or `insertAdjacentHTML()` with untrusted data - Never use `v-html` (Vue), `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (React), or `[innerHTML]` (Angular) with user data - Use framework auto-escaping — do not bypass it - Sanitize HTML if rich text is required (use DOMPurify, bleach, or sanitize-html) - Set Content-Security-Policy headers — at minimum `default-src 'self'` - Set `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, and `SameSite` flags on cookies - Validate URLs before rendering in `href` or `src` — block `javascript:` and `data:` schemes - Use `textContent` instead of `innerHTML` when inserting plain text ### Context-Specific Encoding | Context | Encoding Method | |---|---| | HTML body | HTML entity encode (`<` → `<`) | | HTML attribute | Attribute encode, always quote attributes | | JavaScript | JavaScript hex encode, or use JSON.stringify | | URL parameter | URL encode (`encodeURIComponent`) | | CSS value | CSS hex encode, or use allowlists | ### Framework-Specific Guidance #### React ```jsx // SAFE — React auto-escapes

{userInput}

// DANGEROUS — bypasses escaping

// If rich text needed, sanitize first import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';

``` #### Server-Side Templates ```python # Jinja2 — auto-escapes by default, but watch for: {{ user_input | safe }} # BAD — disables escaping {{ user_input }} # GOOD — auto-escaped # ERB (Ruby) <%= user_input %> # GOOD — auto-escaped in Rails <%== user_input %> # BAD — raw output ``` #### Vanilla JavaScript ```javascript // BAD element.innerHTML = userInput; // GOOD element.textContent = userInput; ``` ### URL Validation ```javascript function isSafeUrl(url) { try { const parsed = new URL(url); return ['http:', 'https:'].includes(parsed.protocol); } catch { return false; } } ```
